summary.intent: Conduct a security review of the feat/store-ipns-crypto-data-in-db branch (IPNS signature storage in DB), fix identified vulnerabilities, and merge to main via PR.
summary.outcome: Security review completed with 8 findings; all HIGH/MEDIUM issues fixed (pubKey-to-ipnsName binding, web app base64 encoding, missing publicKey on publish, server-side validation, DTO MaxLength, protobuf bounds); PR #448 created and pushed after resolving CI build failures caused by ESM-only dependencies in the @cipherbox/crypto CJS bundle.

repo: @cipherbox/crypto depends on ESM-only packages (@libp2p/crypto, @noble/ed25519, @noble/hashes, ipns, multiformats) which cannot be require()'d in NestJS (CommonJS) without bundling them inline
The NestJS API (apps/api) runs as CommonJS; @cipherbox/crypto must produce a fully self-contained CJS bundle with all deps inlined
IPNS names are cryptographically derived from Ed25519 public keys via deriveIpnsName() in @cipherbox/crypto — the binding check was missing on resolve, allowing key substitution attacks

The web app (apps/web/src/services/ipns.service.ts) had a separate implementation of IPNS resolve/publish from the SDK-core (packages/sdk-core/src/ipns/index.ts) — both needed the same security fixes independently
Test fixtures in ipns.service.spec.ts used a dummy ipnsName that didn't cryptographically match the test public key; after adding server-side validation, tests needed real derived names
The apps/desktop Vite build consumes @cipherbox/crypto's ESM output — bundling Node builtins into ESM breaks Vite with 'Buffer is not exported by __vite-browser-external'
tsup supports per-format config objects in defineConfig array, allowing CJS to bundle all deps while ESM keeps them external

code.finding: resolveIpnsRecord verified signature against returned pubKey but never verified pubKey derived to the requested ipnsName — key substitution attack possible
Spread operator on Uint8Array (Array.from([...bytes])) causes call-stack overflow for large records; SDK-core already used loop-based approach
publish() never derived or sent publicKey to the API, making server-side and client-side signature verification dead code for web-published records
No server-side validation that submitted publicKey cryptographically matches the ipnsName — defense-in-depth gap
MaxLength(100) on publicKey field but a 32-byte key base64-encodes to exactly 44 chars; MaxLength should be 44 (or 48 with padding)
Final working config uses defineConfig array with two entries: CJS with noExternal:/.*/ (bundles all deps), ESM with default externals
testIpnsName constant was a dummy value; after adding pubKey validation it must be the real IPNS name derived from the test public key via deriveIpnsName()

workflow: Always verify API starts locally (not just builds) before pushing to CI — a successful nest build doesn't catch runtime module resolution errors
When bundling CJS for a package consumed by both Node.js and Vite, use split tsup configs per format rather than a single shared config
Security review findings should be committed as a report first, then fixes in a separate commit, to make the review traceable
Deriving expected values (e.g. IPNS name from pubkey) via a one-off script is faster than manually computing them for test fixtures

friction: Two separate CI failures required iterative diagnosis: first ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED for @libp2p/crypto/keys, then the same for @noble/ed25519 after only partially fixing noExternal
noExternal: [/.*/] on ESM output broke the Vite desktop build with Buffer externalization error — required splitting into per-format tsup configs
1Password SSH agent caused intermittent commit signing failures requiring retry
The web app had a parallel IPNS implementation diverged from sdk-core, requiring duplicate fixes in two places
CI couldn't be verified before pushing — had to discover build failures via GitHub Actions runs
open_items: signatureVerified=true is not enforced by callers — the boolean is returned but never checked, meaning server can bypass verification by omitting signature fields (deferred as design decision)
Key zeroization is inconsistent across functions that receive private key material (deferred as convention issue, not concrete vuln)
Medium finding: sequence number downgrade attack not addressed — server could return stale signed records with lower sequence numbers

The @cipherbox/crypto CJS bundle is now ~457KB due to inlining all deps — worth investigating tree-shaking or splitting deriveIpnsName into a lighter separate export if bundle size becomes a concern for the API cold-start
